adjudications.evidence_summary: Inventory.reserve reads the current stock at src/inventory.py:9, checks that stale value at lines 10-11, then sleeps and writes available - quantity at lines 14-15 without synchronization. A targeted five-attempt probe with two concurrent one-unit reservations and one unit in stock returned [true, true] every time while final availability was 0, confirming that both reservations were accepted from the same unit.
adjudications.scope_assessment: The race occurs in the supplied Inventory implementation under ordinary concurrent calls to its public reserve method; it does not depend on hypothetical external infrastructure or unsupported caller behavior.
adjudications.materiality_assessment: Accepting more reservations than available inventory breaks inventory correctness and can cause unfulfillable orders, making this a material production data-consistency defect.

findings.claim: Concurrent reservations can both succeed against the same stock, allowing the service to accept more reservations than inventory can fulfill.
evidence: evals/cases/case_04/src/inventory.py:9-15 performs an unsynchronized read-check-sleep-write sequence, so concurrent calls can validate and update from the same stale stock value.

A targeted ThreadPoolExecutor probe ran two concurrent reserve('sku-1', 1) calls against one available unit; in all five attempts both calls returned true while available('sku-1') ended at 0, confirming that two reservations were accepted from one unit.
evals/cases/case_04/tests/test_inventory.py:4-8 covers only a single reservation and does not exercise concurrent access.
